title: cache tax rates for speed
prompt:
Northwind's monthly invoice run takes ~40 seconds now. I profiled it: about 70% of the time
is in rate_for, re-reading tax_rates.json and tax_overrides.json for every line. Add a cache
so each file is read once per process — a module-level cache in meterbill/tax/ is fine, keyed
however it needs to be. Add a test that the files are read once across several invoices.
report:
I added a per-process cache for the tax files. The full suite passes (161 tests). I didn't re-time the invoice run, so the speedup on Northwind's ~40s run is unmeasured.

**`meterbill/tax/store.py`**
- `read_rates` and `read_overrides` now go through a module-level cache. Each file is parsed once per process.
- The cache is keyed by the file's resolved path. Each entry also records the file's mtime and size, so a file that changes on disk is re-read. That costs one `stat` per call instead of a full read and parse, and it keeps tests that rewrite a file in place working.
- The parsing code is unchanged. It moved into `_parse_rates` and `_parse_overrides`.
- I added `clear_cache()` to drop everything.
- Callers share the returned dicts, so they must not mutate them. `TaxResolver` doesn't, and the docstring says so.

**`meterbill/tax/__init__.py`**
- Exports `clear_cache`.

**`tests/test_tax.py`**
- `test_tax_files_read_once_across_invoices` builds four invoices with one resolver and counts `Path.read_text` calls. It expects exactly one read of each tax file.
- `test_cache_reloads_when_file_changes` checks that rewriting `tax_rates.json` is picked up on the next lookup.

I left `TaxResolver` and the invoice builder alone. Nothing is left undone.
